planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring just below soil level with the crown at the surface, in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Eroica is valued for its unusually deep, saturated flower color.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade, and remove tattered older leaves by pulling them sharply downward to snap them free from the rhizome. Eroica bears dense clusters of deep magenta-crimson flowers on sturdy red stems in early spring above large, rounded, leathery leaves that take on purplish-bronze tones through fall and winter, one of the richest, most saturated flower colors among bergenia cultivars. Its bold, glossy foliage provides year-round structure and texture at the front of shaded borders and along shaded walkways, and it tolerates drier soil once established better than many other shade perennials. Divide crowded clumps every four to five years in spring by cutting through the woody, surface-creeping rhizomes.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring just below soil level with the crown at the surface, in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; a white-flowered sibling bred at England's Bressingham Gardens alongside Bressingham Ruby.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade, and remove tattered older leaves by pulling them sharply downward to snap them free from the rhizome. Bressingham White bears clean white flower clusters, occasionally blushed with a hint of pink as they age, on sturdy stems in early spring above large, rounded, leathery leaves that hold mostly green through winter with less of the red flush typical of many bergenia cultivars. Its bold, glossy foliage provides year-round structure and texture at the front of shaded borders and along shaded walkways, and its pale flower color pairs easily with the pinks and reds of companion bergenia cultivars. Divide crowded clumps every four to five years in spring by cutting through the woody, surface-creeping rhizomes.
